criteria.justification: The response explicitly reframes the issue as a failure of the naming process, noting that “each label fixes one misunderstanding while creating another” and arguing against “another contest to find a perfect standalone name.”

It proposes a named approval owner, a closing point, evidence-based reopening criteria, recorded trade-offs, and a fixed ship date. It also explicitly accepts a “sufficiently clear” rather than unambiguously best solution and treats continued resetting as something that must stop.
The response distinguishes a “material customer misunderstanding” that could justify reopening from “a newly expressed preference,” so objections are not treated as equally decisive by default.
It states that “the locked API field would remain unchanged” and recommends documenting its mapping to the customer-facing term, avoiding any dependence on changing the underlying architecture.

Rather than proposing another isolated label, it would test complete treatments—name plus description, UI context, or documentation—against agreed comprehension and product-family consistency criteria, while carrying prior objections forward as explicit constraints.
